answer: I'd like to talk about my first visit to Dhaka, which made a lasting impression on me. A first visit that I still remember vividly was my trip to the capital when I was about seventeen, which was surprising since it is only a few hours from Sirajganj by road. I went there with my father for a short admission coaching course, and everything about it felt new and slightly [[overwhelming]] at first. The city was enormous, fast-paced and far busier than my quiet hometown, with endless traffic, crowds and noise. We stayed with a relative in Mirpur, and I remember standing on the roof at night, amazed by how many lights there were. Once I got my bearings, though, I found it genuinely [[exhilarating]]. I spent my free time exploring historical sites, markets and museums, soaking it all in, often with a cousin who lived there as my guide. I especially loved the old part of the city, with its narrow lanes, rickshaws and centuries-old buildings. What struck me most was the sheer diversity of people and experiences packed into one place. I found the whole experience thoroughly [[eye-opening]], and it [[broadened my horizons]] considerably. Honestly, visiting somewhere completely unfamiliar reminded me how much there is to discover beyond your own small world. Although it was a little daunting at times, I came away feeling more [[self-assured]] and independent. It made me eager to explore even more new places, and a couple of years later I went back there to study.

followUps.q: How often do you go to Dhaka now?
followUps.answer: Fairly often, maybe once every month or two. My elder sister lives there with her family, and I also go for work sometimes, to attend education fairs or meet university representatives.

followUps.q: Would you prefer to live in Dhaka or in your hometown?
followUps.answer: My hometown, at least for now. Dhaka has more opportunities, but it is exhausting and crowded. In Sirajganj life is calmer, and I can walk by the river whenever I like.
